title: Accepted MIME set and per-file size cap are elicited per project; no shelf default beyond "nothing accepted"
context: A shelf blueprint cannot know what a downstream project's upload endpoint accepts. A photo-gallery product accepts a narrow image set (jpeg, png, webp) with a 20 MB per-file cap; a document workspace accepts pdf, docx, txt with a 100 MB cap; a code-review product accepts a broad set with a 5 MB cap. Picking a default that fits all projects picks one that fits none. Shipping without any elicited values leaves the input TAC in a state where every file is refused (the safe default), which is the correct floor: a project that forgets to elicit the accepted set discovers this immediately on the first upload.
decision: The accepted MIME set and the per-file size cap are elicited per project through this ADR. The blueprint contributes the two parameters as elicits on apply; the input TAC's MIME gate refuses every file until both are elicited. The elicited MIME set is a list of IANA media types; wildcards (image/*, application/*) are permitted for projects that want them but discouraged in the guide. The per-file size cap is a positive integer in bytes. A concurrency cap and the announcer cadences are secondary elicits with recommended defaults owned by `TAC-2403.interfaces.tickInterval` (250 ms internal poll, not user-observable) and `TAC-2403.interfaces.announcementInterval` (2 seconds user-observable announcement cap); concurrency defaults to 3.
consequences: Projects that apply the blueprint without elicitizing discover the refusal on the first upload attempt and go through the elicit flow to unblock it; the refusal is legible ("MIME gate has no accepted set") rather than silently accepting everything. Projects with a mature accepted-set list paste it in once and never revisit. The pack asserts the input TAC refuses an obvious wrong-MIME file (a text/plain payload with a jpeg extension) and refuses a payload exceeding the size cap.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ship a broad default set (image/*, application/pdf, text/plain)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Adopt a shelf default that covers the most common cases so most projects can apply without elicitizing.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Any default that is broad enough to be useful is broad enough to be wrong for a project whose backend cannot accept the same set; the discovery cost of a mismatched accepted set at the server is higher than the discovery cost of the refuse-all floor at the client.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ship no accepted-set gate at all
alternativesConsidered.summary: Rely on the server to refuse a wrong-MIME upload and skip the client-side gate.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The server refusal happens after the bytes are on the wire; a client that never gates wastes the operator's upload budget on payloads the server will refuse and loses the aria-describedby error binding the input TAC ships.
